selection: Lexicographically first successful occurrence in each of two prescribed inputs; selection recorded before detailed inspection, after aggregate phase-one outcomes were known.
execution: Verified source modules executed with in-memory boundary substitutes; full application and production-frequency claims are outside this check.

checks.observation: A watcher can miss continuation creation before its baseline and emit an incorrect corrective message. Reversing that ordering prevents the message.
checks.limitation: The real database, poller and full lifecycle were not executed.

checks.observation: An earlier acknowledgement can clear a newer local intent; a subsequent send can then fall back to persisted state.
checks.limitation: Send resolution and intent persistence share a mutex. The isolated execution does not establish whether the adverse request ordering is reachable through the real application.

interpretation: These checks illustrate evidence quality and limits. They do not estimate adjudicator precision or establish human ground truth. Observed examples are exposed regression candidates, not unseen holdouts.
